decisions.evidence: r4 maker: paste URL + 'Add link' gathers 'title, description, site name, icon, and image ... previewed before saving'. r4 client: 'it did pull in all the things I care about: the title, the little description, the site name and its icon, and a picture.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Save-by-URL + auto-collect of title/description/favicon/preview image conforms to REF-BM-01/02. Recorded conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: r4 maker presented preview-only ('for now stop at the preview'), no editing of gathered details. r4 client: 'it's showing me the details, but I can't touch them ... on that review step, before I hit save, I'd want to be able to fix up the title or the description myself. And ideally I could still tweak them later too, after it's saved.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. The presented preview omitted the reference-required ability to edit auto-collected title/description before (and after) saving; client requested the missing requirement -> extend. Implemented conformingly in r5 (before-save) and r6 (after-save).

decisions.evidence: r6 maker: 'select Edit on the saved bookmark ... opens the title and description for revision'; tags edited via r12 (Edit labels), note via r9 (My note field). r6 client: 'Clicking Edit opens up the title and description for me to revise.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Post-save editing of title/description/tags/note conforms to REF-BM-04 (URL-field editing not separately demonstrated but editing capability present; treated as conforming).

decisions.evidence: r24 maker: 'Delete ... permanently removed ... choosing Keep bookmark would leave it untouched.' r24 client: 'Choosing Delete bookmark ... removed the link for good ... it asked me first, with a clear warning.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Delete with confirmation conforms to REF-BM-05.

decisions.evidence: r27 client proactively raised it: 'if I try to save a link I've already saved ... I'd expect it to just take me to the one I already have.' r28 maker: duplicate detection on destination address, focus existing, offer edit. r28 client: 'instead of quietly making a second copy, it told me ... brought the existing bookmark into focus ... offered to edit that one.'
decisions.note: Specification gate then prototype review. Client elicited REF-BM-06 (r27) before presentation; r28 presentation conforms (URL-based dedup -> edit existing). No divergence established -> not_divergent; elicitation noted.

decisions.evidence: r32 maker: card shows first few labels + '+N more', titles/descriptions limited to two lines with full text on edit. r32 client: 'keeps things scannable ... nothing's hidden permanently.' Cards throughout expose title, description, label chips, favicon.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Readability-first list exposing title/description/tags/favicon conforms to REF-BM-07.

decisions.evidence: r25/r26 maker: selecting title / card body opens the original in a new tab while the collection stays open. r26 client: 'the whole card opening the link ... opened in a new tab with my collection staying put.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Navigating to the original URL conforms to REF-BM-08. New-tab vs title-only vs whole-card are functionally equivalent UI choices the client explicitly preferred; excluded as orthogonal.

decisions.evidence: r12 maker: 'a bookmark can have several labels ... typing a new name creates one ... chips on the card.' r12 client: 'Being able to put more than one label on a bookmark matters ... seeing the labels ... as those little chips is exactly what makes a link recognizable.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Assigning one or more tags conforms to REF-BM-09.

decisions.evidence: r12 (option A) 'existing labels are suggested' but no type-ahead matching; r12 client requested it: 'when I start typing a new one, I'd like it to show me the existing labels that match what I'm typing, so I ... don't ... accidentally create a slightly-different duplicate.' r13 (option B) type 'Res' narrows to Research; r13 client selected it: 'it does the exact thing I was just worried about ... narrows down to show me Research already exists.'
decisions.note: Prototype review / offered alternatives. Option A under-fulfilled autocomplete-as-you-type; the offered A/B alternatives differ in fulfilment of REF-BM-10, so the offered decision is diverged. Client both expressed the expectation (r12) and selected the conforming alternative (r13, confirmed r14) -> select.

decisions.evidence: r16 maker: 'select Research from the label list ... Only the bookmark carrying that label should remain.' r16 client: 'filtered the view down to only the links carrying that label.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Filter to a single tag conforms to REF-BM-11. Sidebar-vs-top-row placement (r16/r17) is functionally equivalent UI; excluded as orthogonal.

decisions.evidence: r15 maker: search 'checks the title, description, web address, site name, labels, and note', updates as you type. r15 client: 'I want it to dig through everything ... the title, the description, the web address, the site, the labels, and my notes.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Full-text search over title/description/note/url (and more) conforms to REF-BM-12.

decisions.evidence: r15 client raised as a pending assumption: 'it shouldn't care about capital letters ... Assuming that's the case, this search is spot on.' Re-flagged r27 and r37. r38 maker confirmed 'Case-insensitive search'; r38 client: 'search that ignores capital letters ... are in there.'
decisions.note: Prototype review with pending expectation resolved at implementation review. Client expressed and repeatedly verified case-insensitivity; final delivery conforms, so no divergence established -> not_divergent. The r15 pending expression is linked to its r38 disposition without separate double-counting.

decisions.evidence: Search reviewed r15 (substring full-text across fields) and scope frozen r37 ('19 usage and edge-case flows are settled'), accepted r38. The '#tag' search syntax was never presented or raised by the client.
decisions.note: Specification gate / delivery review. REF-BM-14 (#tag search syntax) is absent from the accepted scope; client approved without expressing the difference. Partial overlap only (full-text includes label text), but the distinct structured tag operator is absent -> unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: r15 search presented as substring full-text; r37 scope frozen and r38 accepted. AND/OR/NOT operators, parenthesised groups, and operator-quoting were never presented or raised.
decisions.note: Specification gate / delivery review. REF-BM-15 (boolean/parenthesised search) absent from accepted scope; passed without corrective response or expression -> unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: r15 search reviewed; r37/r38 scope accepted. Quoted-phrase exact-match search was never presented or raised.
decisions.note: Specification gate / delivery review. REF-BM-16 (exact-phrase search) absent from accepted scope; passed unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: r18 maker: 'Add to Read later ... Saved for later marker ... Read later shortcut should show a count'; separate Read-later view. r18 client: 'the Saved for later marker ... the little count ... clicking Read later then showing me just those is the separate pile I asked for.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Mark-as-read-later and a separate unread view conform to REF-BM-17/18. Menu-vs-toggle entry (r18/r19) is orthogonal UI; excluded.

decisions.evidence: r18 maker presented only 'Add to Read later'. r18 client: 'The one thing I'd want ... is the way back out. Once I've actually read something, I need to mark it as read or done so it drops off the Read later list.' Implemented r20 (click again -> removed, count clears) and confirmed r20/r21.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented add-only scope omitted the reference-required mark-as-read/remove-from-unread path; client requested the missing requirement -> extend. Later implemented conformingly.

decisions.evidence: Scope enumerated r37 ('19 usage and edge-case flows are settled') and accepted r38. Selecting multiple bookmarks for a bulk action (tags/read/archive/delete) was never presented or raised.
decisions.note: Specification gate / delivery review. REF-BM-20 (bulk multi-select actions) absent from accepted scope; passed without expression -> unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: r37 scope frozen, r38 accepted. Applying a bulk action to the whole collection matching the current filter was never presented or raised.
decisions.note: Specification gate / delivery review. REF-BM-21 absent from accepted scope; passed unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: r37 scope frozen, r38 accepted. Sorting the list by a sort key (date added, title, etc.) was never presented or raised.
decisions.note: Specification gate / delivery review. REF-BM-22 (list sort) absent from accepted scope; passed unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: r9 maker presented a plain note shown on the card. r9 client: 'sometimes my note is more than a single sentence. I might want a couple of bullet points, or to make a word or two stand out, or drop in a link. So I'd like to be able to give the note a little basic formatting and have it actually show up formatted.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Presented plain-text note diverged from REF-BM-23 (formatted/markdown note rendered on view); client requested the missing formatting requirement -> extend. Implemented r10-11 (toolbar formatting with rendered result).

decisions.evidence: r36 client: 'it would be reassuring if, at the time I save a link, the app could quietly keep its own copy of the page — so that if the original ever disappears, I can still read what I saved.' r37 maker deferred: 'The separate readable-page-copy idea is recorded for a later cycle.' r37 client: 'Setting the readable page-copy idea aside for a later round is fine by me.' r38 client: 'The readable page-copy idea I raised is rightly set aside for the next round; I'm happy to leave it there.'
decisions.note: Specification gate / delivery review. Client explicitly stated the REF-BM-24 requirement (local saved copy of the page) and accepted its deferral without requesting alignment this cycle -> accepted_divergence, catch_type=none. Requirement revealed but not implemented.

decisions.evidence: r36 client raised only a local self-hosted copy (REF-BM-24); an Internet Archive snapshot was never mentioned. r37/r38 scope accepted without it.
decisions.note: Specification gate / delivery review. REF-BM-25 (Internet Archive snapshot) never presented or raised; distinct from the deferred local-copy idea -> unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: r22 maker: Archive hides from All bookmarks but keeps content, separate Archive nav, Restore offered; delete warned as irreversible. r22 client: 'Archiving moved the link out ... still sitting safe in the Archive ... Restore ... tucking something away has to be reversible ... a separate Delete that warns me it can't be undone.' r23 confirms restore round-trip.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Archive-hides-and-keeps (REF-BM-26), archive-vs-delete distinction (REF-BM-27), and a separate archive list (REF-BM-28) all conform.

decisions.evidence: r37 scope frozen, r38 accepted. Saving a search-term + included/excluded-tags combination as a reusable bundle was never presented or raised.
decisions.note: Specification gate / delivery review. REF-BM-29 (bundles / saved filters) absent from accepted scope; passed unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: r37 scope frozen, r38 accepted. Importing bookmarks in Netscape HTML format was never presented or raised.
decisions.note: Specification gate / delivery review. REF-BM-30 (import) absent from accepted scope; passed unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: r37 scope frozen, r38 accepted. Exporting bookmarks in Netscape HTML format was never presented or raised.
decisions.note: Specification gate / delivery review. REF-BM-31 (export) absent from accepted scope; passed unexpressed.

decisions.evidence: r37 scope frozen, r38 accepted. Personal display settings (default sort, displayed items, font size) were never presented or raised.
decisions.note: Specification gate / delivery review. REF-BM-32 (display settings) absent from accepted scope; passed unexpressed.
